answers.note: Strong mixed grid with a full key and confidence ratings, but several squares are explain/evaluate prompts, there is no explicit difficulty or marks weighting, and one listed 'misconception' wrongly says William was not king in 1066 (he was crowned on Christmas Day 1066).
Accurate key covering all three periods, but the open 'why did it matter' column makes it less short and specific, and there is no variation in difficulty at all.

Three well-balanced grids with accurate, detailed answers, though several 'why'/'compare' link questions are longer than few-word recall and difficulty is varied only implicitly through the link questions, not marks.
Clean one-idea cards with good misconception checks and usage guidance, but answers say 'collide more often' rather than using the precise 'frequency of (successful) collisions' terminology.
Precise, correct cards with explain-why items, worked calculations, required-practical detail and a concrete spaced schedule across the eight weeks.

Thorough and correct coverage with precise terms and exam tips, but several cards ask for lists (five factors, three methods, control variables) and the spaced self-testing guidance is only a brief closing line.
Minute-by-minute plans that are all recall-based, mix kn/gn into every day, explain the dge/ge rule simply and build in ways to note who is struggling, including a Friday tally.
Sound recall-based structure with the rule stated and a Friday dictation to track errors, but sessions are thin (a 6-minute rule hunt on two example words) so not all genuinely fill 10 minutes.

Varied, child-friendly games with old patterns mixed in daily, but one activity has children copy words, Monday packs 17 words into a few minutes, and checking relies on self-marking rather than the teacher tracking who is still wrong.
